tutorial.label: ECCV 2026 Tutorial
tutorial.title: Efficient MLLM Inference via Approximate and Exact Computing.
tutorial.summary: Multimodal large language models are powerful but expensive to serve. This tutorial presents a systematic view of efficient inference through two complementary lenses: approximate computing that removes model and data redundancy while preserving practical utility, and exact computing that improves systems and hardware execution without changing model outputs.

topics.title: Model Compression
topics.summary: Quantization, sparsity, and low-rank decomposition for reducing model redundancy in MLLM inference.

topics.title: Token Efficiency
topics.summary: Training and training-free compression methods for long multimodal inputs and autoregressive generation.

topics.title: System-Level Design
topics.summary: Exact computing methods and inference frameworks that improve throughput and latency without changing the computed result.

introduction_html: The ENCODE Lab at Westlake University, led by Dr. Huan Wang, will present 4 papers accepted to ICML 2026 — spanning speculative decoding, RL-guided KV cache compression, dense-to-MoE conversion for visual generation, and one-shot pruning of state-space models. See you at COEX!

papers.title: Prism-MoE: Efficient Dense-to-MoE Conversion for Visual Autoregressive Generation
papers.authors_html: Ying Li, Zefang Wang, Zhaode Wang, Zhiwen Chen, Chengfei Lv, Huan Wang
papers.summary_html: Transforms pretrained dense visual autoregressive models into sparse MoE models at low cost: trajectory-consistent initialization casts expert init as a principled decomposition that preserves the pretrained generation trajectory, and confidence-adaptive sparse fine-tuning aligns expert specialization with visual token information density. Under 10% of the standard training budget, dense-level quality with only 37.5% active parameters.
papers.session: TUE · Jul 7 · 2:00–3:45 PM | Hall A · Poster #2611

papers.title: ARC-Decode: Accelerated Decoding with Risk-Bounded Acceptance
papers.authors_html: Ying Li, Zhaode Wang, Zhiwen Chen, Chengfei Lv, Huan Wang
papers.summary_html: Speculative decoding under sampling (T>0) over-rejects low-risk drafts, so real speedups lag greedy decoding. ARC-Decode is a training-free relaxed-acceptance rule: a Jensen–Shannon-divergence risk bound plus confidence-based pre-verification accepts drafts that provably preserve the target distribution. Plugged into EAGLE-3, up to 1.6× end-to-end speedup under sampling with negligible quality change.
papers.session: TUE · Jul 7 · 2:00–3:45 PM | Hall A · Poster #2815

papers.title: RLKV: Which Heads Matter for Reasoning? RL-Guided KV Cache Compression
papers.authors_html: Wenjie Du, Li Jiang, Keda Tao, Xue Liu, Huan Wang
papers.summary_html: Reasoning LLMs are fragile to KV cache compression during long chain-of-thought generation. RLKV uses reinforcement-learning probing to identify the small set of attention heads that keep reasoning coherent, giving them full KV cache while aggressively compressing the rest — 20–50% cache reduction at near-lossless accuracy and up to 1.21× speedup.
papers.session: TUE · Jul 7 · 10:30 AM–12:15 PM | Hall A · Poster #1610

papers.title: SparseSSM: Efficient Selective Structured State Space Models Can Be Pruned in One-Shot
papers.summary_html: The first training-free pruning framework extending optimal brain surgeon (OBS) to state-space architectures: a second-order saliency score aggregates Hessian-trace information across time steps for the time-shared SSM transition matrix, with component sensitivity analysis guiding FFN pruning. Prunes 50% of Mamba SSM weights with no zero-shot accuracy loss and no fine-tuning — state-of-the-art for Mamba-based LLMs.
papers.session: WED · Jul 8 · 2:30–4:15 PM | Hall A · Poster #1014

introduction_html: The ENCODE Lab at Westlake University (advised by Dr. Huan Wang) has 6 papers accepted to CVPR 2026 — spanning efficient multimodal LLMs, visual reasoning, autoregressive generation, and 3D model quantization. Four of the six are led by first-time authors. See you in Denver!

papers.title: OmniZip: Audio-Guided Dynamic Token Compression for Fast Omnimodal LLMs
papers.authors_html: Keda Tao, Kele Shao, Bohan Yu, Weiqiang Wang, Jian Liu, Huan Wang
papers.summary_html: A training-free, “listen-to-prune” framework for omnimodal LLMs: salient audio tokens guide the pruning of video tokens, so audio and video are compressed jointly. Up to ~3.4× faster inference and ~1.4× lower memory with near-baseline accuracy and no retraining.
papers.session: SAT · Jun 6 · 11:45 AM–1:45 PM | ExHall F · Poster #320

papers.title: EarlyTom: Early Token Compression Completes Fast Video Understanding
papers.authors_html: Hesong Wang*, Xin Jin*, Lu Lu, Chenhaowen Li, Jian Chen, Qiang Liu, Huan Wang  *equal contribution
papers.summary_html: Vision encoding itself dominates time-to-first-token, so EarlyTom does training-free token compression early — inside the vision encoder — rather than only late in prefilling. With a decoupled spatial token-selection strategy it cuts TTFT by up to 2.65× and FLOPs by up to 61% on LLaVA-OneVision-7B at near-full-token accuracy.
papers.session: SUN · Jun 7 · 3:30–5:30 PM | ExHall A · Poster #405

papers.title: StreamingTOM: Streaming Token Compression for Efficient Video Understanding
papers.authors_html: Xueyi Chen, Keda Tao, Kele Shao, Huan Wang
papers.summary_html: A training-free, two-stage framework for streaming video. Causal Temporal Reduction caps per-frame tokens before the LLM; Online Quantized Memory keeps the KV-cache in 4-bit with on-demand retrieval. ~15.7× KV-cache compression and ~2× faster time-to-first-token vs. prior SOTA, with memory bounded regardless of stream length.
papers.session: SAT · Jun 6 · 4:45–6:45 PM | ExHall A & F · Poster #302

papers.title: QVGGT: Post-Training Quantized Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
papers.summary_html: The first post-training quantization framework for VGGT-style feed-forward 3D reconstruction. Per-block sensitivity drives mixed-precision allocation; token filtering with camera-information compensation tames outlier camera/register tokens; a task-aware scale search preserves cross-head geometric consistency. Near-lossless W4A16 with 3–4.9× memory reduction and up to 2.8× speedup — bringing 3D perception to edge devices.
papers.session: FRI · Jun 5 · 4:00–6:00 PM | ExHall A & F · Poster #34

papers.title: Parallel Jacobi Decoding for Fast Autoregressive Image Generation
papers.authors_html: Boya Liao, Ying Li, Siyong Jian, Huan Wang
papers.summary_html: Autoregressive image models are slow because they emit tokens one at a time. PJD reframes decoding as a Jacobi iteration that refines many tokens in parallel, cutting the number of sequential forward passes needed per image and speeding up generation.
papers.session: FRI · Jun 5 · 4:00–6:00 PM | ExHall A & F · Poster #171

papers.title: ReasonMap: Towards Fine-Grained Visual Reasoning from Transit Maps
papers.authors_html: Sicheng Feng, Song Wang, Shuyi Ouyang, Lingdong Kong, Zikai Song, Jianke Zhu, Huan Wang, Xinchao Wang
papers.summary_html: A benchmark of 1,008 human-verified QA pairs over high-resolution transit maps from 30 cities in 13 countries, jointly probing fine-grained visual understanding and spatial reasoning. A two-level metric scores answer correctness and route quality; evaluating ~16 MLLMs surfaces a counterintuitive open- vs. closed-source reasoning-model gap.
papers.session: SUN · Jun 7 · 3:30–5:30 PM | ExHall A · Poster #454
